citation: Rudd, P., Aguilera, A. B. V., Elliott, L., & Chambers, B. (2017). MathsFlip: Flipped Learning. Evaluation Report and Executive Summary. London: Education Endowment Foundation. (Evaluation conducted by the Institute for Effective Education / NFER team.)
report_number: EEF project: MathsFlip (Flipped Learning), April 2017; ERIC ED581151
design: Cluster (school-level) RCT, efficacy trial, business-as-usual control; 24 schools randomised in 12 matched pairs (12 intervention / 12 control); analysis sample 1,129 pupils (542 intervention; 587 control), 24 schools; Years 5-6 (KS2, ages 9-11; US-coded grade band 3-6); subject primarily mathematics (with reading/writing/APS as secondary spill-over outcomes); 3-level multilevel model (Pupil within School within matched Pair). Outcomes are KS2 fine-grade scores from the National Pupil Database.
problems: Primary academic outcome (KS2 maths) IS academic, so no non-academic flag needed; intervention is teacher PD (Shireland staff trained Year 5 teachers over 2 days + ongoing support to deliver flipped-learning maths). The report explicitly reports Hedges' g for each contrast (Table 4), computed per Hedges (2007) for cluster-RCTs: adjusted mean difference (accounting for pairing, controlling for the corresponding KS1 covariate) divided by the UNADJUSTED total SD of the KS2 outcome -> taken directly as g, pretest- and cluster-adjusted. Impact SE not printed; derived from each reported 95% CI as SE = CI_width/(2*1.96) (normal approximation; CI midpoints exactly equal the reported g, confirming symmetric CIs). CAVEAT: the MLM used degrees of freedom based on number of schools (~22 df, 12 matched pairs), so the report's CIs are likely t-based on school-level df; using the normal approximation may slightly understate SE/Var (this matches the convention used in sibling EEF extractions in this repo, e.g. jay_2017). ICC = 0.16 is the analysis-stage design ICC (Table 3), not a per-outcome observed ICC; protocol ICC was 0.15; pre-post correlation^2 = 0.52 at analysis. NEVER guessed an ICC. n_t/n_c are the analysis (n-in-model) pupil counts per arm. Note registry coded the outcome test as 'Res/Dev' (researcher/developer-made); however the actual outcome instrument used is the national KS2 SATs fine-grade score (a standardized/independent national assessment), so test_type is labelled standardized_independent. The reading/writing 'effect' was larger than the maths effect; the report itself cautions this is likely chance given only 24 schools and no plausible mechanism. Subgroup analyses (Table 5: Ever-FSM g=0.10, boys g=0.06, girls g=0.13, low achievers g=-0.01, medium g=0.20, high achievers g=-0.03, all KS2 maths, all non-significant) are non-randomised subsets -> NOT extracted as full-sample records; only the 4 full-sample primary/secondary contrasts are extracted.

effect_sizes.arm_label: MathsFlip flipped-learning teacher PD (single TPD arm) vs business-as-usual control
effect_sizes.test_name: KS2 mathematics fine-grade score (National Pupil Database / KS2 SATs)
effect_sizes.timepoint: post (summer 2015, end of Year 6 KS2 assessment, ~1 year after intervention delivery in Year 5)
effect_sizes.g_method: Reported directly as Hedges' g (Table 4). Computed by evaluator per Hedges (2007) for cluster-RCT: adjusted (pair-accounting, KS1-maths-covariate) mean difference between arms / unadjusted total SD of KS2 maths outcome. Taken as g. SE derived from reported 95% CI (-0.28, 0.46): SE = (0.46-(-0.28))/(2*1.96) = 0.1888; g_var = SE^2.
effect_sizes.page_ref: p.18 Table 4 (KS2 Maths fine grade); also p.4 exec-summary Summary of impact on main outcomes
effect_sizes.notes: PRIMARY headline/confirmatory outcome. Maths -> STEM per spec. p = 0.62 (not significant). Raw means 29.10 (int) vs 28.68 (ctrl); per-arm posttest SDs not printed (only 95% CIs of the means), so sd_t/sd_c left null. EEF '1 additional month's progress', moderate security (3 padlocks; 2 lost because trial powered to MDES 0.37 > EEF 0.2 max).

effect_sizes.arm_label: MathsFlip flipped-learning teacher PD (single TPD arm) vs business-as-usual control
effect_sizes.test_name: KS2 reading fine-grade score (National Pupil Database / KS2 SATs)
effect_sizes.g_method: Reported directly as Hedges' g (Table 4). Adjusted mean difference (controlling for KS1 ReadWrite covariate, accounting for pairing) / unadjusted total SD of KS2 reading outcome (Hedges 2007 cluster method). SE derived from reported 95% CI (-0.13, 0.57): SE = (0.57-(-0.13))/(2*1.96) = 0.1786; g_var = SE^2.
effect_sizes.notes: SECONDARY spill-over outcome. Reading -> Reading per spec. p = 0.21 (not significant). Covariate = KS1 ReadWrite score. Report cautions the larger literacy effects are likely chance (no plausible mechanism for a maths intervention; only 24 schools). n=546/587 contributing to model.

effect_sizes.g_method: Reported directly as Hedges' g (Table 4). effect_sizes.notes: SECONDARY spill-over outcome. Writing -> Other per spec. p = 0.17 (not significant). Covariate = KS1 ReadWrite score. Same chance-finding caveat as reading. n=546/587 contributing to model.

effect_sizes.arm_label: MathsFlip flipped-learning teacher PD (single TPD arm) vs business-as-usual control
effect_sizes.test_name: KS2 Average Point Score (aggregate across KS2 subjects; National Pupil Database)
effect_sizes.g_method: Reported directly as Hedges' g (Table 4). Adjusted mean difference (pair-accounting, KS1 covariate) / unadjusted total SD of KS2 Average Point Score (Hedges 2007 cluster method). SE derived from reported 95% CI (-0.20, 0.62): SE = (0.62-(-0.20))/(2*1.96) = 0.2092; g_var = SE^2.
effect_sizes.notes: SECONDARY outcome that is a COMPOSITE aggregate across KS2 subjects (subsumes the maths/reading/writing components extracted separately) -> outcome_role=composite, mapped to Other. p = 0.30 (not significant). Likely double-counts the other rows for this study; flag for central de-duplication. n=545/587 in model.
